samples.summary: TextEditor selection walk still indexes body blocks with context-aware indices — header/footer Tab/indent mutates the wrong blocks or crashes
samples.evidence: This delta fixed the cursor-only path (`siblingsOf`, line 2869) to use `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` instead of `document.blocks`, but the multi-block-selection branch of the same walker three lines earlier still does `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks;` (line 2836) while `startIdx`/`endIdx` come from `this.doc.getBlockIndex()`, which is context-aware (`document.ts:271-273` → `getContextBlocks()`). With the caret in a header/footer (a state the delta explicitly declares supported and exercises via the new test) and a cross-block selection, indices resolved against `header.blocks` are used to index `document.blocks`: (a) if the body has fewer blocks than that index, `topLevel[i]` is `undefined` and `b.type` throws a TypeError inside handleTab/handleIndent (`fn(b, topLevel)` at 2849, and `handleIndent`'s own walk at 2754-2759 calls `block.style.marginLeft`), and (b) if the body is long enough, `applyListLevelChanges`/`applyBlockStyle` rewrite unrelated BODY blocks' listLevel/marginLeft while the selected header items are left untouched — a silent wrong-document mutation. The sibling implementation in `editor.ts` was written correctly (`const contextBlocks = doc.getContextBlocks();`, editor.ts:1689/1702), so the two walkers are now out of sync.

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed: `forEachBlockInSelection`'s multi-block branch takes `startIdx`/`endIdx` from the context-aware `doc.getBlockIndex()` (document.ts:271-273 → getContextBlocks(), which returns header.blocks/footer.blocks) but indexes `this.doc.document.blocks` (text-editor.ts:2836). With the caret in a header/footer and a cross-block selection, `topLevel[i]` is either `undefined` (TypeError on `b.type` at 2839, or on `block.style.marginLeft` at 2757 inside handleIndent's callback) or a wrong BODY block that gets its listLevel/marginLeft rewritten while the selected header blocks are untouched. The path is reachable: header/footer edit context is a supported state (setEditContext 402-407) with multi-block selection explicitly handled elsewhere (deleteSelection 3780-3810), and Tab (1120-1122 → handleTab 2680-2705) plus Cmd+]/Cmd+[ (1309/1315 → handleIndent/handleOutdent 2750-2778) reach it with no `editContext === 'body'` gate. The cursor-only fix at siblingsOf (2863-2873) is unreachable for this case because the selection branch returns at 2852. The sibling walker in editor.ts:1689/1702 correctly uses getContextBlocks(), confirming the divergence. Correctness lane (crash / silent wrong-document mutation), severity critical.

finding.summary: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` returns the body blocks even when editing header/footer, so Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ on a header or footer list item becomes a silent no-op
finding.evidence: `siblingsOf` (text-editor.ts:2863-2869) does `if (!info) return this.doc.document.blocks;` — the *body* array. But `TextEditor` supports header/footer editing (`this.editContext`, `getActiveLayout()` at 4579, `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` used everywhere else, and `Doc.getBlock` searches `_document.header?.blocks` separately at document.ts:207). For a caret on a list item in the header, `forEachBlockInSelection` now calls `fn(cursorBlock, this.doc.document.blocks)`; `planSiblingGroup` then scans that body array for `selectedIds.has(block.id)` and never finds the header block, so it returns zero changes and `applyListLevelChanges` writes nothing. Before this change `handleTab`/`handleIndent` called `setBlockType(b.id, …)` directly and worked in any context. Note editor.ts's twin `siblingsOf` (editor.ts:1616) correctly uses `doc.getContextBlocks()` — the two implementations disagree.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim is false. `TextEditor.siblingsOf` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2863-2873 does NOT contain `return this.doc.document.blocks;` — line 2869 reads `if (!info) return this.doc.getContextBlocks();`, preceded by an explicit comment (lines 2865-2868) about the caret sitting in a header/footer list. `Doc.getContextBlocks()` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:158-162) returns `_document.header?.blocks` / `_document.footer?.blocks` per `editContext`, so the cursor-only path in `forEachBlockInSelection` (text-editor.ts:2855-2856) hands `planSiblingGroup` (packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:57,116) the correct container when editing a header/footer, and Tab/Cmd+]/Cmd+[ is not a no-op there. The claimed divergence from editor.ts is also absent: editor.ts:1618-1627 uses `doc.getContextBlocks()` identically, so the two implementations agree rather than disagree. A grep for `this.doc.document.blocks` in text-editor.ts returns no hit anywhere in 2855-2873 (nearest are 2669 and 2836). Line 2836 in the multi-block selection branch is a different path with a different mechanism (context-relative indices from getBlockIndex into the body array) and is not what this finding describes or locates.

finding.summary: Toolbar indent/outdent mutate descendant blocks that are never passed to `markDirty`, so the incremental layout cache repaints them at their old list indent
finding.evidence: `applyListLevelChanges` now rewrites `listLevel` on nested children that lie *outside* the selection, but the only `markDirty` calls come from `forEachBlockInSelection`, which visits selected blocks only (editor.ts:1698, 1707). `indent()`/`outdent()` then call `render()` without `invalidateLayout()`. In `computeLayout` a block that is not in `dirtyBlockIds` reuses cached lines (layout.ts:535-536), and the list indent is baked into the laid-out lines via `effectiveBlock.style.marginLeft = marginLeft + LIST_INDENT_PX * (listLevel + 1)` (layout.ts:493-501, 543). So an unselected child that just moved a level keeps its previous indentation on screen until some later full relayout. `text-editor.ts` avoids this by calling `invalidateLayout()`; `editor.ts` does not.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that "the only markDirty calls come from forEachBlockInSelection", leaving level-changed descendants outside the selection un-dirtied. That is not the code in this repository: applyListLevelChanges itself calls markDirty for every planned change inside its loop (editor.ts:1600-1611), i.e. for the selected roots AND the nested children that planSiblingGroup adds to the plan (list-level.ts:76-81). Blocks inside table cells are mapped to their tableBlockId (editor.ts:1609), the same convention forEachBlockInSelection uses (editor.ts:1660/1680/1713), and tables are re-laid unconditionally anyway (layout.ts:506-529). The dirty set is honored on the exact path cited: render() -> recomputeLayout() (editor.ts:2252-2253) passes dirtyBlockIds to computeLayout (editor.ts:1523-1535), and the cache-reuse branch (layout.ts:535-536) skips reuse for any block in that set, so each mutated block is re-laid with the updated LIST_INDENT_PX * (listLevel + 1) margin (layout.ts:493-501, 538-546). Per-block dirtying makes the absence of invalidateLayout() harmless for this scenario, so the described stale-indent repaint cannot occur as claimed.
